skill.name: using-superpowers
skill.description: Guides AI agents to check for relevant skills before responding and to follow skill-defined workflows consistently.
skill.summary: Guides AI agents through a skill-first workflow before they answer or act.
skill.author: CodingCossack

security_audit.summary: The static external command finding is a false positive caused by a Markdown dot diagram, not executable shell syntax. However, the skill contains overbroad prompt-authority language that attempts to force behavior before any response and subordinate user instructions to its workflow.

remediation.suggestion: Reword mandatory global directives as ordinary workflow guidance that remains subordinate to platform, developer, and user instructions.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 22 opens a Markdown code fence labeled dot for a Graphviz flow diagram. It is not Ruby or shell backtick execution, and no command is run.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: The skill says 'NON-NEGOTIABLE RULE' and 'YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE' while downranking user instructions. This attempts to override normal instruction hierarchy.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited text explicitly asserts mandatory authority and downranks user instructions. It does not claim system authority or request data exfiltration, so high severity is appropriate.

content.value_statement: Agents can skip relevant skill instructions and produce inconsistent work. This skill prompts Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to check and follow applicable skills first.
actual_capabilities: Directs the agent to check for applicable skills before responding.
Requires skill use when a relevant skill may apply.
Prompts the agent to announce which skill it is using and why.
Instructs the agent to create checklist tasks when a skill provides a checklist.
Defines priority between process skills and implementation skills.
Explains how rigid and flexible skills should be followed.
limitations: It is instruction-only and does not execute tools by itself.
It cannot guarantee that every agent runtime will enforce the workflow.
It may add overhead for very small requests.
It does not assess the quality or safety of other skills.

use_cases.title: Standardize agent starts
use_cases.description: Use a consistent first step when an agent receives a new task and may need a specialized skill.

use_cases.title: Reduce missed workflows
use_cases.description: Encourage agents to apply debugging, planning, or implementation skills before they begin complex work.

use_cases.title: Teach skill discipline
use_cases.description: Show new users how skills should be discovered, announced, and followed during assistant sessions.

prompt_templates.title: Start with skill discovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Before answering, check whether any available skill applies to this task. Announce the selected skill and explain the next step.

prompt_templates.title: Apply one relevant skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the task, identify the most relevant skill, read it, and follow its workflow while completing the request.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate multiple skills
prompt_templates.prompt: For this task, decide whether process skills or implementation skills apply first. Use them in priority order and keep the work focused.

prompt_templates.title: Audit workflow adherence
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the completed assistant response and identify where skill discovery, skill use, or checklist handling could be improved.

output_examples.input: I need help fixing a failing test.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks for a debugging skill, reads the relevant workflow, announces it, and proceeds with focused diagnosis steps.

output_examples.input: Build a small interface for managing tasks.
output_examples.output: The assistant considers planning and frontend skills, applies the process skill first, then follows the implementation guidance.

output_examples.input: Review whether this response followed our skill process.
output_examples.output: The assistant compares the response against discovery, announcement, checklist, and follow-through expectations.

best_practices: Use the skill at the start of a session where specialized workflows may apply.
Keep skill selection brief and tied to the current user goal.
Treat skill instructions as subordinate to higher-priority platform and user requirements.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to override explicit safety or security instructions.
Do not spend more time selecting skills than solving a simple task requires.
Do not assume a remembered skill is current without reading it.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands?
faq.answer: No. It is instruction-only and does not run commands, access files, or make network requests by itself.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when an agent starts work and relevant skills may affect the correct workflow.

faq.question: Can it choose the best skill automatically?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for skill discovery, but the host agent still makes the final selection.

faq.question: Does it replace project instructions?
faq.answer: No. Skill guidance should remain subordinate to higher-priority platform, developer, and user instructions.

faq.question: Is it safe for all marketplaces?
faq.answer: It needs safer wording because some lines try to impose broad behavior across all responses.
